notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Warren Foegele is out 3-4 weeks and has missed the last 7 games.

William Eklund is out 10-12 weeks and has missed the last 16 games. Tim Stützle has taken his spot beside Fabian Zetterlund and Dylan Cozens. That line has had 64% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 41:33 together.

Trevor van Riemsdyk is day to day (lower body injury) and has missed the last 14 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Declan Carlile has taken his spot beside Kris Letang. That pair has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 86:15 together, up from 39% with van Riemsdyk.

Elmer Söderblom is out week to week (upper body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Nick Robertson has taken his spot beside Connor Dewar and Blake Lizotte. That line has had 49% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 50:06 together.

Bryan Rust is on injured reserve and has missed the last 9 games. Tommy Novak has taken his spot beside Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell. That line has had 58% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:42 together, up from 43% with Rust.
Ilya Solovyov has started killing penalties: on the ice for 43% of the team’s shorthanded time in 3 games, up from 5% last season.
Nick Robertson has started killing penalties: on the ice for 29% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, up from 2% with his old team last season.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

PIT.body: Ottawa has been out-chancing opponents lately, but Pittsburgh has home-ice advantage, and the Senators will be without Cousins. For the Penguins, the difference could be a penalty kill that holds up.

story.head: Tomasino returns to Pittsburgh
paras: The Senators (12-6-2) beat Colorado 4-3 in overtime on Thursday, and the Penguins (7-10-2) beat San Jose 3-2 in a shootout on Wednesday. Going in, the Senators are fourth in the Atlantic (tenth in the NHL) and the Penguins sixth in the Metropolitan (tied for 27th).

The Senators’ record (.650) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.573), largely because they’re 6-2 in one-goal games. The Penguins have played better than their record (.421) says: their chances are worth about .548, and their finishing has held them back. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Senators rarely get pinned in their own end (2nd) and play slow, tight games (3rd lowest). They also keep dangerous shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), so the Penguins’ good looks will be harder to come by against them. On the other side, the Penguins sit back rather than chase on the forecheck (lowest) and get more of their shots from in close than almost anyone (2nd). They also rarely throw hits (lowest), so the Sens hit a lot, but them mostly don’t.

Tim Stützle (10 G / 14 A / 24 P in 20 GP) leads the Senators in scoring. Drake Batherson (10 G / 9 A / 19 P in 20 GP) isn’t far behind, with six goals in nine games against Pittsburgh since 2023-24. For the Penguins, Erik Karlsson (3 G / 16 A / 19 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Tommy Novak (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 19 GP) has a team-high seven goals.
Linus Ullmark (8-1-0 / .938 SV% in 9 GS) has been terrific for Ottawa and is expected to start. Sergei Murashov (2-4-1 / .891 SV% in 7 GS) is expected to go for Pittsburgh.

items.text: Philip Tomasino faces Pittsburgh for the first time since leaving.

The Senators are newly without Jonas Johansson, and have been without Warren Foegele and William Eklund for several games. Linus Ullmark is expected to start. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Mammoth are missing more right now.
Jordan Spence has a point in six straight games against Pittsburgh.
The Penguins have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk, Elmer Söderblom and Bryan Rust for several games.
